newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by BOJ operation, Nikkei.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by BOJ operation, Nikkei.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures fell on sales of Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Monday as the market shed some of its recent euphoria following the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s less than generous money market operation.
"The BOJ drained 200 billion yen from the market today and people had been looking for them to drain 100 billion yen," a trader with a European futures house said.
"There was a lack of news and the market's been a bit overbought so some profit-taking came in," he added.
The expiry of the June Euroyen contract and heavy offers from a U.S bank from 124.19 in September JGBs also depressed the market, he said.
December Euroyen stood at 99.08 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close, also its day high, of 99.11. Volume was a low 8,400 lots.
The contract is expected to trade a 99.08-99.12 range in the near term, with gains increasingly capped ahead of the BOJ's quarterly tankan survey of business sentiment next week.
September JGBs ended at 123.94 after hitting a high of 124.21 against their previous close at 124.01.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed with interest focused on the U.S. May Consumer Price Index, due on Tuesday.

"After the retail sales figures last week, everybody is looking for rates not to be hiked in July," the trader said, referring to the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting next month, where expectations of a rate hike are fading.
"It looks like the Eurodollars are going to be stuck here for a while but I'd like to buy on any dips to 93.92/93 in December," he said.
December Eurodollars ended steady against their IMM close at 93.965.
